To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the modification of PMCA2 or PMC3 isoforms in PC12 cells resulted in increased MGST1 activity, which may represent an adaptive response against increased Ca2+ cytotoxicity.
suppression of PMCA2 or PMC3 isoforms in PC12 cells resulted in increased activity of microsomal GSTs, and that this effect is mediated by formation of MGST1 oligomeric forms.

the suppression of plasma membrane calcium pump isoforms--PMCa2 and PMCa3--leads to increased expression and formation of hexamers of MGST1, which is associated with higher GSH levels and protection against cytotoxicity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of PMCA2 or PMA3 suppression on MGST1 expression, activity and oligomeric state in PC12 cells.
the adaptation of MGST1 expression to the modified PMCA isoform content in PC12 cells.
the role of MGST1, its regulation and possible function in the cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the suppression of PMCA isoforms in the plasma membrane leads to the increase of MGST1 activity, which is probably due to an increased amount of MGST1 protein.

the PMCA3 reduction leads to increased MGST1 expression in PMCA3-suppressed PC12 cells, while PMCA2 reduction leads to increased expression of MGSTs, which is not necessarily related with MGST1 expression.
PMCA2/3 suppression in PC12 cells leads to increased MGST1 expression, which may be an adaptive response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MGST1 may be an important factor in the protection against Ca2(+)-induced cytotoxicity.
PMCA2 and PMCA3 are involved in regulation of MGST1 activity in PC12 cells.
MGST1 is a membrane protein with a high degree of plasticity that can adapt to changes in its environment, and that this plasticity is a part of the cellular defense mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PMCA2 and PMCA3 are involved in the regulation of MGST1 expression and its oligomeric forms in PC12 cells.
the PMCA activity is a key factor in the regulation of MGST1 activity and expression in PC12 cells, and that MGST1 hexamer is a functional form of the enzyme.
MGST1 is a potential target for the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases, and that the modification of PMCA isoforms may serve as a tool in the development of novel neuroprotective agents.
